result.summary:
Turn 92 closed the run's local work on the exhausted capacities, with the frontier reduced to a short documented residue.

Why a scoped stop rather than more work. Two capacities are exhausted: audit units (no further obligation can be opened) and semantic reviews, which means the newest artifact — the end-to-end client-reply scenario for the owner-alive re-proposal protection, executed as 6baf5b7715294d88a8f4a36e085ebd04 — cannot receive the correspondence review that would confirm it and therefore stays visible as an unreviewed execution rather than being claimed. Experiments and calls remain, but the frontier is no longer unexplored code: every file named in the run's analysis roots has been read, the map is current at version 19, and the outstanding items are deployment or framework questions rather than investigation targets. The stop is scoped to the focus, so unfinished units and disputes remain visible instead of being closed by it.

Where the audit stands. Twelve claim families were established, each with its own obligation, bindings, plan and executed artifacts: nine confirmed violations or consequences — C1 (a recovery ignores a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED and commits a NOOP vector for it, on a driven proposal/commit history), C3 (the same divergence reaching the applied state, also on a driven history), C2 (the durable metadata record loses the bal value it writes), C4 (a legal NOOP commit terminates a restarted owner through a nil dereference, on a constructed history), C6 (the same recovery divergence for the deployment's promoted replica), C7 (the accept handler's rejection branch is unreachable, so a rejected round waits for the timeout), C9 (the recorder writes the recovering replica's own row's metadata, or dereferences nothing), C10 (a value beyond the 16-bit length field is truncated, displaces the following commands, and panics the receiver's decoder), C11 (replica construction dereferences a failed probe dial, so an environment without a route to the probe cannot start a replica), C12 (the documented transitive-conflict skipping is inert) — plus two bounded no-violation protections: C5 (an owner that survives a NOOP recovery re-proposes the operation and, as of the newest artifact, answers the client end to end) and C8 (the executor's timeout enqueues a blocked instance and the enqueued entry starts a real recovery).

Residue recorded rather than absorbed. The reader-side reaction to a displaced stream cannot be exercised from an in-package harness because the replica package's listener is unexported, so it stays a source-based inference. Whether a deployment enables the latency file, durable recording or the transitive-skip flag decides whether those findings are live, and that is a configuration question. Two candidates remain paused with scoped resume conditions (accept-status semantics, client retry), and one attribution issue on the superseded C1 artifact has no mechanism the validator accepts, so it remains visible as bookkeeping with its substance already recorded in the amended claim and in C3. Resume conditions for the stopped focus name the missing review capacity, the unit capacity a new obligation would need, and the configurations that would activate the remaining paths.

question.question: When a replica receives PreAccept for instance (Replica, Instance) while its local record for that instance already has Status >= ACCEPTED but stores no commands, handlePreAccept writes the received command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] instead of the addressed instance InstanceSpace[preAccept.Replica][Instance]. Is any legal history able to put a replica in that state with preAccept.LeaderId != preAccept.Replica, and if so does the addressed record (Replica, Instance) stay without commands (halting its row's execution and the recovery replies about it) while an unrelated record (LeaderId, Instance) acquires a command that no quorum committed for it?
question.importance: Wrong-slot attribution of a command mutates protocol state without any quorum behind it: a record that never committed that command can become executable as though it had, while the record the message was addressed to can be left permanently unexecutable because executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and findSCC returns false for a command-less instance. Both effects are consensus-visible (an uncommitted command can reach the state machine, and a committed instance can stop making progress).
contexts: instance owned by replica R and led by replica L != R (recovery re-proposal)
instance owned and led by the same replica (normal proposal) as the control that must behave identically
event_paths: deliver PreAccept(LeaderId=L, Replica=R, Instance=i, Ballot=b, Command=c, Seq, Deps) to a replica whose InstanceSpace[R][i] has Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil
compare the record that receives Cmds after the handler returns against the record named by (Replica, Instance)

supporting_behavior_ids.B5-slow-path-accept: shows that the accept phase stores accepted attributes on followers without any status transition, which is the premise the >= ACCEPTED branch would need
supporting_behavior_ids.B11-prepare-resolution: re-runs pre-accept on behalf of another replica's instance, which is the only read path in which PreAccept.LeaderId differs from PreAccept.Replica
supporting_behavior_ids.B12-try-preaccept: another recovery path that re-sends a command for an instance owned by a different replica
supporting_behavior_ids.B7-execute-scheduler: shows the execution requirement Cmds != nil that makes a command-less record of the addressed instance a permanent row stall

counterevidence: scoped to the writers of Instance.Cmds and Instance.Status read in this snapshot: no path sets Status >= ACCEPTED together with Cmds == nil, because the leader-side transitions copy lb.cmds in the same step (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply) and handleCommit copies commit.Command (S13-handleCommit)

scoped to the wire format used between replicas: a nil command slice is marshalled as a zero-length prefix and unmarshalled as a non-nil empty slice, so a Commit cannot install a nil Cmds while setting COMMITTED (S13-handleCommit)

scoped to the accept path: handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps and leaves Status unchanged, so an acceptor holds no accepted status; the only records with Cmds == nil are fresh default records with Status NONE (S11-handleAccept, S14-recovery-start-prepare, S13-handleCommit)
unknowns: whether the accept phase is required to record an ACCEPTED status on the acceptor that stores accepted attributes, since the guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts and recovery sub-case 2 presuppose that some replica reports ACCEPTED

whether handlePrepareReply's value selection may adopt a reply whose Status is NONE at the highest vbal (an acceptor that stored no commands) instead of an equal-vbal reply that carries the pre-accepted value
question.trigger_rationale: Source reading showed the discrepancy directly: S9-handlePreAccept uses preAccept.Replica at lines 782, 792-798, 810, 816 and 828-829, but preAccept.LeaderId at line 809 for the same object. The state needed to reach the branch (Status >= ACCEPTED with nil Cmds on a replica receiving a PreAccept) is not produced by any path read: handleAccept stores bal/vbal/Seq/Deps without recording ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept), the leader-side ACCEPTED/COMMITTED transitions set Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), handleCommit installs commit.Command (S13-handleCommit), and a marshalled nil command slice comes back as a non-nil empty slice. The reachability premise is therefore resolved as not produced, and the separated remaining premise is whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED.

question_candidates.stop_reason: Source review resolved the Candidate's discriminator without needing execution. The wrong-slot write at epaxos/epaxos.go:809 assigns the received command to InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance], but every other access in handlePreAccept addresses the instance named by the message, (preAccept.Replica, preAccept.Instance). The premise that branch needs -- a local record with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil -- is not produced by any status-advancing path in the snapshot: handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but leaves Status at NONE; the leader-side accept and commit transitions (handlePreAcceptReply, handleTryPreAcceptReply, handleAcceptReply) copy lb.cmds and set the command in the same step as the status; handleCommit copies commit.Command, which arrives through the wire format where a nil slice is unmarshalled as a non-nil empty slice; and the only records with nil Cmds are freshly created defaults with Status NONE. The branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance, which is why the wrong-slot write is not reachable today. The map is updated in the same product: Behaviors B3 and B5 record the sourced protection and the answered unknown, and core_overview's first open detail is replaced by the sourced conditional relationship. The remaining, now separated, premise -- whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED on an acceptor, which three guards and one recovery sub-case presuppose -- is carried in feedback for a later question.

question.question: handlePreAcceptReply commits when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and inst.lb.allEqual && allCommitted && isInitialBallot, but for r.N <= 3 with Thrifty the reply-wise equality result is discarded (the allEqual accumulator is never updated), so with N = 3 the leader fast-commits its own (seq, deps) after a single reply whose recomputed attributes may differ. Can such a commit leave two attribute vectors for one instance at the same vbal -- the leader's committed vector and the fast-quorum peer's pre-accepted vector -- so that a later recovery, which selects the reply with the highest vbal by iterating the reply slice with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot, can adopt the peer's vector instead of the committed one; and does the legal crash point between the leader's local fast commit and bcastCommit make that reachable while some replica has already executed the committed vector?
question.importance: If reachable, one instance is committed with different (seq, deps) at different replicas, so the same command is ordered differently against conflicting commands on different replicas; execution then applies the same commands in different orders, the surviving replicas' state diverges, and a reply already produced under the old order is contradicted. That is a consensus-safety consequence (agreement and state-machine convergence), not a performance or liveness one.
participants: instance leader (owner of the instance row)
one fast-quorum peer that recomputed different attributes
recovering replica that later runs prepare for the instance
contexts: N = 3 with Thrifty (the configuration replica.New hardcodes and run.go passes through unchanged)
fast path with exactly FastQuorumSize-1 = 1 reply whose attributes differ from the leader's
leader crash after the local fast commit but before the Commit broadcast is delivered
event_paths: leader starts phase 1 for its own instance with deps d1/seq s1 and sends PreAccept to one peer
peer recomputes d2 != d1 (or s2 != s1) against its own conflict index and replies PREACCEPTED
leader adds the reply, skips the allEqual update because N <= 3 and Thrifty, and commits its own d1/s1, then broadcasts Commit
recoverer runs prepare and selects the candidate value among replies with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot
compare the (Seq, Deps) the recoverer re-commits with the vector the leader committed

supporting_behavior_ids.B3-preaccept-recipient: establishes the peer's differently recomputed attributes and the PREACCEPTED reply that carries them
supporting_behavior_ids.B9-recovery-trigger: shows when a leader or peer that holds an uncommitted or committed record initiates recovery of the instance
supporting_behavior_ids.B11-prepare-resolution: shows the highest-vbal selection that decides which vector is re-proposed
supporting_behavior_ids.B7-execute-scheduler: shows that execution applies the committed vector and that a reply can already have been produced before the divergence becomes visible

counterevidence: scoped to the fast-path branch: the source comment states there is no need to check equality for N <= 3 with Thrifty (S10-handlePreAcceptReply), so an author argument for the exemption may exist even though it is not written down

scoped to quorum arithmetic: for N = 3 a fast quorum of FastQuorumSize = 2 is already a majority, so the exemption may be intended to rely on fast-quorum/slow-quorum intersection instead of attribute equality (S21-quorum-sizes)

scoped to project documents: the README states that the bundled EPaxos is the corrected version and that thriftiness is required for correct recovery, which suggests the N = 3 thrifty configuration was deliberately exercised (S27-readme)
unknowns: whether a recovery-led phase 1 can leave the merged committed vector's leader-row component below the peer's record, and whether the peer's larger component can be re-committed by a recovery that reaches the peer rather than the committed leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether that requires the recovering leader to have lost its own row knowledge, which the launched configuration permits only through a restart because Durable is false and no reader of the stable store exists (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos)
question.trigger_rationale: The exemption is explicit in the source: in handlePreAcceptReply the equality result computed by mergeAttributes is only accumulated in the else branch, so for r.N <= 3 && r.Thrifty inst.lb.allEqual keeps its initial true value from newLeaderBookkeeping (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S2-instance-bookkeeping). With FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2 = 2 for N = 3 (S21-quorum-sizes) and the commit condition preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1, one disagreeing reply is enough to commit the leader's own vector. The candidate pairs the commit with the recovery rule that must reconstruct the same value: handlePrepareReply keeps the attributes of the reply with the highest vbal (S15-handlePrepareReply), so two vectors at one vbal are the discriminator. A controlled multi-replica schedule is the check that could distinguish an actual same-vbal split from the author's intended majority-intersection argument.

history.question: handlePreAcceptReply commits when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and inst.lb.allEqual && allCommitted && isInitialBallot, but for r.N <= 3 with Thrifty the reply-wise equality result is discarded (the allEqual accumulator is never updated), so with N = 3 the leader fast-commits its own (seq, deps) after a single reply whose recomputed attributes may differ. Can such a commit leave two attribute vectors for one instance at the same vbal -- the leader's committed vector and the fast-quorum peer's pre-accepted vector -- so that a later recovery, which selects the reply with the highest vbal by iterating the reply slice with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot, can adopt the peer's vector instead of the committed one; and does the legal crash point between the leader's local fast commit and bcastCommit make that reachable while some replica has already executed the committed vector?
history.importance: If reachable, one instance is committed with different (seq, deps) at different replicas, so the same command is ordered differently against conflicting commands on different replicas; execution then applies the same commands in different orders, the surviving replicas' state diverges, and a reply already produced under the old order is contradicted. That is a consensus-safety consequence (agreement and state-machine convergence), not a performance or liveness one.

question_candidates.stop_reason: Sourced review answers the Candidate's discriminator instead of leaving it open. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given, starting from the deps vector carried in the message and skipping the row of the instance owner named in that message, so a pre-accepting peer returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise. With one counted peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's componentwise merge therefore equals that peer's vector in every compared component, and mergeAttributes ignores only the leader's own row. In an owner-led instance the peer skips exactly that row, so the merged vector equals the peer's record and the fast-commit branch installs the same vector on the leader: both members of the fast quorum hold the committed vector at the same vbal, and any recovery quorum the recoverer can assemble (self plus one reply, with both remaining replicas being fast-quorum members) contains a holder. That mechanism is what keeps the exemption from publishing an unsupported vector, so the proposition is explained. The surviving exposure is confined to one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes keeps the leader's own row value while the peer may have raised it; it requires the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader, and it is recorded as the remaining premise. The map is updated in the same product (B4's unknown and the N<=3 open detail) so the earlier, over-broad phrasing does not mislead the next question.

question.question: handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal for instance (Replica, Instance) and never writes inst.Status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept holds accepted attributes with Status NONE, and one that did see it keeps PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ. Does any decision depend on an accepted record carrying status ACCEPTED: can a later PreAccept for the same instance overwrite the accepted attributes because handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard cannot fire, and can a recovery that should re-accept an already accepted value instead take the phase-1 restart path because handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 needs a reply whose Status is ACCEPTED?
question.importance: An acceptor that stores accepted attributes without recording that it accepted them can (a) have those attributes recomputed by a later PreAccept at the same or a higher ballot instead of being preserved, and (b) hide from a recovering leader the fact that the value reached the accept phase, which is the distinction between re-proposing the accepted value and starting a fresh phase 1. Either effect can change the value a majority eventually commits for the instance, which is agreement-relevant rather than cosmetic; the accept phase is also the only place where a value is fixed without commands being stored, so a wrong reconstruction can also drop a command that only some replicas hold.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept); which histories reach that branch is unresolved.

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply documents six sub-cases but the guards for sub-cases 3 and 4 are textually identical, so the TryPreAccept-based sub-case appears unreachable (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept).
handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1 (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
after.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

selections.rationale: Source review resolved the Candidate's discriminator without needing execution. The wrong-slot write at epaxos/epaxos.go:809 assigns the received command to InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance], but every other access in handlePreAccept addresses the instance named by the message, (preAccept.Replica, preAccept.Instance). The premise that branch needs -- a local record with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil -- is not produced by any status-advancing path in the snapshot: handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but leaves Status at NONE; the leader-side accept and commit transitions (handlePreAcceptReply, handleTryPreAcceptReply, handleAcceptReply) copy lb.cmds and set the command in the same step as the status; handleCommit copies commit.Command, which arrives through the wire format where a nil slice is unmarshalled as a non-nil empty slice; and the only records with nil Cmds are freshly created defaults with Status NONE. The branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance, which is why the wrong-slot write is not reachable today. The map is updated in the same product: Behaviors B3 and B5 record the sourced protection and the answered unknown, and core_overview's first open detail is replaced by the sourced conditional relationship. The remaining, now separated, premise -- whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED on an acceptor, which three guards and one recovery sub-case presuppose -- is carried in feedback for a later question.

feedback.answered: The Candidate's discriminator is resolved on sources: no legal history in the captured snapshot establishes the branch premise. A replica that receives PreAccept can hold Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil only if some local transition sets ACCEPTED, COMMITTED or EXECUTED without also installing commands. handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but never writes Status, so an acceptor that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE even though it holds accepted attributes (S11-handleAccept). Every transition that does set Status >= ACCEPTED also sets Cmds in the same handler: handlePreAccept stores the received command when it sets PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ (S9-handlePreAccept), the leader-side accept and commit paths set inst.Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), and handleCommit copies commit.Command (S13-handleCommit). A commit command cannot arrive as nil through the wire format: Marshal writes a zero-length prefix and Unmarshal allocates a non-nil empty slice. The only nil-Cmds records are fresh default records with Status NONE (S11-handleAccept, S13-handleCommit, S14-recovery-start-prepare). The line 809 branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance, and the wrong-slot write cannot be reached; the two sourced discrepancies (the LeaderId index and the omitted ACCEPTED status) currently compensate instead of composing into a defect.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

selections.rationale: Sourced correction and frontier cleanup while the N<=3 fast-path Candidate stays active. Reading handlePreAcceptReply again showed that the committed vector is not the leader's own proposal vector: the merged (seq,deps) produced by mergeAttributes are written back into the leader bookkeeping (lb.deps/lb.seq = merged while lb.status <= PREACCEPTED_EQ) before the branch is chosen, and both the fast-commit branch and the accept branch then install that merged vector. The N<=3 Thrifty exemption therefore does not change which vector is published; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equals that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either certifies agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. The Candidate's premise is corrected accordingly, and the exposure is now stated precisely: the leader's own record keeps the proposal ballot as vbal while a pre-accepting peer records the same pre-accept ballot, so a recovery selecting by vbal cannot prefer the committed vector over a strictly smaller one held by a peer. In the same product, the two recovery open details are resolved as unreachable dead code in the map (sub-case 4 never runs, taking with it bcastTryPreAccept, handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply, the possibleQuorum bookkeeping and the deferMap check), and B4 now records the merge-installation guard.

feedback.answered: Two sourced results. formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. selections.rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). In that owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum, so a recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) must intersect one of them and sees the committed vector. The exemption is therefore not automatically unsafe. The case that can split is a phase 1 restarted for an instance whose owner is another replica (handlePrepareReply sub-case 5 or 6 calls startPhase1 with PreAccept.Replica = owner and LeaderId = recovering replica, S15-handlePrepareReply, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1). There the leader and the peer both skip the owner's row but raise their own rows from their own conflict tables, so the leader can contribute a component on its own row that the peer does not have while the peer contributes another: the merged vector is then strictly greater than either record and is held only by the committing leader, while the peer keeps its smaller vector at the same ballot (S9-handlePreAccept, S10-handlePreAcceptReply).
remaining: whether a recovery whose slow quorum contains the differing peer rather than the committed leader re-proposes the peer's smaller vector for the instance (the highest-vbal selection cannot separate them because both records carry the pre-accept ballot as vbal) (S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether the already-committed leader then refuses the later Commit and keeps the larger vector, freezing two committed vectors for one instance (handleCommit returns early for Status >= COMMITTED) (S13-handleCommit)
whether the two vectors order conflicting instances differently, since the difference is a dependency component on a row whose conflicting command may not yet be committed at the peer (S20-exec)

whether the recovery-led fast commit is reachable with a single peer reply inside the exempted configuration, that is whether an N=3 deployment with a non-owner recovery is a supported history (S24-runReplica-epaxos, S21-quorum-sizes)
feedback.rationale: This refines, rather than replaces, the earlier correction: the merged vector is what gets committed, and the question is whether any other replica holds it at the same vbal. The owner-led case is now explained (a single peer's vector dominates and is adopted by both), which is consistent with the source comment that equality need not be checked there. The recovery-led case remains open and is the discriminator a controlled schedule would settle; recording it here keeps the map stable and leaves the Candidate's proposition intact while making the next construction step concrete. Nothing in the requirement, the observed behaviors or the previously explained Candidate is weakened.

selections.rationale: Sourced review answers the Candidate's discriminator instead of leaving it open. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given, starting from the deps vector carried in the message and skipping the row of the instance owner named in that message, so a pre-accepting peer returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise. With one counted peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's componentwise merge therefore equals that peer's vector in every compared component, and mergeAttributes ignores only the leader's own row. formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

The recovery side is already confirmed (claim C1) and its applied effect is confirmed (claim C3), so the remaining unexplored consequence is the client contract: the proposal lived only on the original leader, the re-propose branch is guarded to the committing replica's own row, and replies are produced at execution under the launched configuration. feedback.answered: The client-side half of the question is answered on sources: the captured client has no retry and no reply deadline. SendProposal writes each proposal once (to the leader, or to the closest replica in the leaderless EPaxos configuration of run.go) and never re-sends it (S29-client-sendproposal). The reply path is a blocking read: WaitReplies loops on GetReplyFrom(waitFrom) and only leaves the loop when the read returns an error such as net.ErrClosed, at which point it logs and stops rather than re-sending (S28-client-waitreplies, S30-client-getreplyfrom). There is no timeout, no outstanding-request table and no CommandId-based retransmission, so a proposal whose instance was committed as NOOP by a recovery is never completed on either side: the recovering replica never held the proposals (it preserves only its own record's clientProposals), the re-propose branch requires the commit to land on the committing replica's own row with a single NONE command (S13-handleCommit), and the client does not re-issue the request.
remaining: whether the replica side could be expected to complete another replica's proposal, i.e. whether the recovering replica should adopt the owner's proposals when it recovers the owner's row (no read path does)

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

feedback.answered: The question is answered in two parts on sources. Where the owner survives and processes the NOOP commit, the admitted operation is kept alive: the reviewed check for claim C5 confirmed that the owner installs the commit and re-proposes the operation onto the propose channel (artifact fb1d0e558f4641c7850fe8aaca4068df: pending cleared, one proposal waiting). feedback.answered: B14's unknown about what sets IsLeader is answered: the master owns that flag. At registration it marks one replica as leader - the alias named by the config's Leader field, or, when no Leader is configured, the replica with the lowest ping RTT measured by the master's ping command - and reports IsLeader to it; during master startup and again whenever its ping loop finds a leader dead, it calls Replica.BeTheLeader on the marked replica via HTTP RPC (S31-master-startup, S32-master-register).
