formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement. The same masking holds when the recovering replica is the replica the deployment promoted to leader (IsLeader true, so makeBallot raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot): the promoted-variant check for claim C6-recovery-ignores-committed-reply-when-promoted confirmed in scope that the committed reply is still skipped and the NOOP vector committed, and the accept handler's own rejection branch for a higher-ballot AcceptReply is unreachable because the ballot-equality gate returns first (claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection, confirmed in scope), so a rejected round waits for the timeout-driven recovery.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleAcceptReply returns whenever a reply's ballot differs from the round's, so the nack branch behind that gate never runs and a peer that answers with a higher ballot is ignored rather than counted as a rejection; the direct check for claim C7 confirmed nacks 0 and no reaction, and the pre-accept side has no rejection signal either (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so progress after a rejection depends on the 10s execution timeout rather than on the handlers (S12-handleAcceptReply, S11-handleAccept, S4-execute-loop).

handleAcceptReply returns whenever a reply's ballot differs from the round's, so the nack branch behind that gate never runs and a peer that answers with a higher ballot is ignored rather than counted as a rejection; the direct check for claim C7 confirmed nacks 0 and no reaction, and the pre-accept side has no rejection signal either (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so progress after a rejection depends on the 10s execution timeout rather than on the handlers (S12-handleAcceptReply, S11-handleAccept, S4-execute-loop).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement. The same masking holds when the recovering replica is the replica the deployment promoted to leader (IsLeader true, so makeBallot raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot): the promoted-variant check for claim C6-recovery-ignores-committed-reply-when-promoted confirmed in scope that the committed reply is still skipped and the NOOP vector committed, and the accept handler's own rejection branch for a higher-ballot AcceptReply is unreachable because the ballot-equality gate returns first (claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection, confirmed in scope), so a rejected round waits for the timeout-driven recovery.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. feedback.answered: A codec contract break is reproduced locally: the value codec frames a command's value length in two bytes on both sides, while the client's command size is configuration-driven (aws.conf sets 1000, and the field allows up to 65535). Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement. The same masking holds when the recovering replica is the replica the deployment promoted to leader (IsLeader true, so makeBallot raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot): the promoted-variant check for claim C6-recovery-ignores-committed-reply-when-promoted confirmed in scope that the committed reply is still skipped and the NOOP vector committed, and the accept handler's own rejection branch for a higher-ballot AcceptReply is unreachable because the ballot-equality gate returns first (claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection, confirmed in scope), so a rejected round waits for the timeout-driven recovery.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo. Progress when a round is rejected does not come from the handlers: the direct check for claim C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance confirmed that the executor's per-row timeout enqueues the blocked instance for recovery after roughly twelve seconds of wall clock, so a stalled row is recovered by the timeout path rather than by a rejection signal.

Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo. Progress when a round is rejected does not come from the handlers: the direct check for claim C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance confirmed that the executor's per-row timeout enqueues the blocked instance for recovery after roughly twelve seconds of wall clock, so a stalled row is recovered by the timeout path rather than by a rejection signal.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).

handleAcceptReply returns whenever a reply's ballot differs from the round's, so the nack branch behind that gate never runs and a peer that answers with a higher ballot is ignored rather than counted as a rejection; the direct check for claim C7 confirmed nacks 0 and no reaction, and the pre-accept side has no rejection signal either (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so progress after a rejection depends on the 10s execution timeout rather than on the handlers (S12-handleAcceptReply, S11-handleAccept, S4-execute-loop).

with recording enabled, the phase-1 entry records metadata through the recovering replica's own row while installing the instance under the owner's row, so a recovery-led phase 1 either records a different instance's ballot context or terminates on an absent record; the direct check for claim C9-durable-recorder-uses-the-instance-row confirmed the nil dereference with Durable true and an empty own row, and the case where that slot exists is still unread (S8-handlePropose-startPhase1, S19-durable-record).

the command value codec frames a value's length in a two-byte field on both sides, while the client's command size is configuration-driven; the three direct checks for claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire confirmed in scope that a 70000-byte value is written as 70013 bytes but decoded as 4464 bytes with 4477 consumed, that the command following such a value in the same buffer decodes to garbage (op 197, an arbitrary key and a 53198-byte value), and that decoding a real PreAccept carrying such a value panics with makeslice: len out of range, which the receiver's reader has no recover for. The default configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary, and what a participant does after a displaced stream is unread (S37-state-value-codec, S38-client-command-size, S22-replica-listener).
after.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

feedback.answered: The client-side half of the codec finding's applicability is answered: the client caps nothing. feedback.answered: The delay-ordering helper's semantics are now understood and its one dangerous premise is bounded. When a latency table is configured, client proposals are passed through a per-connection ordering structure that hands proposals to the replica's propose channel only in a contiguous run starting from CommandId zero (the traversal compares the last handled id with the next node's id minus one, starting from -1). A connection whose first proposal carries any other CommandId would therefore never be delivered: the proposal sits in the structure and the client waits. The premise does not arise in this snapshot: the client numbers its proposals from zero (seqnum initialised to -1 and incremented before use) and creates one connection per run, and although Reconnect exists in the client it has no call site anywhere in the repository, so no connection is ever reused with a continuing command-id sequence.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement; the strongest of those checks drives the committed record itself from a real proposal, PreAccept round and commit broadcast before the recovery runs. formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement; the strongest of those checks drives the committed record itself from a real proposal, PreAccept round and commit broadcast before the recovery runs. The same masking holds when the recovering replica is the replica the deployment promoted to leader (IsLeader true, so makeBallot raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot): the promoted-variant check for claim C6-recovery-ignores-committed-reply-when-promoted confirmed in scope that the committed reply is still skipped and the NOOP vector committed, and the accept handler's own rejection branch for a higher-ballot AcceptReply is unreachable because the ballot-equality gate returns first (claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection, confirmed in scope), so a rejected round waits for the timeout-driven recovery.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo. Progress when a round is rejected does not come from the handlers: the direct check for claim C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance confirmed that the executor's per-row timeout enqueues the blocked instance for recovery after roughly twelve seconds of wall clock, so a stalled row is recovered by the timeout path rather than by a rejection signal. The applied-state consequence of that divergence is confirmed on the same driven history: the direct checks for claim C3-applied-effect-follows-committed-vector show that the recovering replica applies nothing for the instance's key while the replicas holding the real committed vector apply it, so the disagreement between committed vectors also reaches the state machines (artifacts f1d4a9f06e81464aa803ee7809e4e5c6 and 52a176deb66c4588a59d71f8afeb13ab).

question.question: When a replica receives PreAccept for instance (Replica, Instance) while its local record for that instance already has Status >= ACCEPTED but stores no commands, handlePreAccept writes the received command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] instead of the addressed instance InstanceSpace[preAccept.Replica][Instance]. Is any legal history able to put a replica in that state with preAccept.LeaderId != preAccept.Replica, and if so does the addressed record (Replica, Instance) stay without commands (halting its row's execution and the recovery replies about it) while an unrelated record (LeaderId, Instance) acquires a command that no quorum committed for it?
question.importance: Wrong-slot attribution of a command mutates protocol state without any quorum behind it: a record that never committed that command can become executable as though it had, while the record the message was addressed to can be left permanently unexecutable because executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and findSCC returns false for a command-less instance. Both effects are consensus-visible (an uncommitted command can reach the state machine, and a committed instance can stop making progress).

instance owned and led by the same replica (normal proposal) as the control that must behave identically

compare the record that receives Cmds after the handler returns against the record named by (Replica, Instance)

history.question: When a replica receives PreAccept for instance (Replica, Instance) while its local record for that instance already has Status >= ACCEPTED but stores no commands, handlePreAccept writes the received command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] instead of the addressed instance InstanceSpace[preAccept.Replica][Instance]. Is any legal history able to put a replica in that state with preAccept.LeaderId != preAccept.Replica, and if so does the addressed record (Replica, Instance) stay without commands (halting its row's execution and the recovery replies about it) while an unrelated record (LeaderId, Instance) acquires a command that no quorum committed for it?
history.importance: Wrong-slot attribution of a command mutates protocol state without any quorum behind it: a record that never committed that command can become executable as though it had, while the record the message was addressed to can be left permanently unexecutable because executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and findSCC returns false for a command-less instance. Both effects are consensus-visible (an uncommitted command can reach the state machine, and a committed instance can stop making progress).

question.question: handlePreAcceptReply commits when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and inst.lb.allEqual && allCommitted && isInitialBallot, but for r.N <= 3 with Thrifty the reply-wise equality result is discarded (the allEqual accumulator is never updated), so with N = 3 the leader fast-commits its own (seq, deps) after a single reply whose recomputed attributes may differ. Can such a commit leave two attribute vectors for one instance at the same vbal -- the leader's committed vector and the fast-quorum peer's pre-accepted vector -- so that a later recovery, which selects the reply with the highest vbal by iterating the reply slice with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot, can adopt the peer's vector instead of the committed one; and does the legal crash point between the leader's local fast commit and bcastCommit make that reachable while some replica has already executed the committed vector?
question.importance: If reachable, one instance is committed with different (seq, deps) at different replicas, so the same command is ordered differently against conflicting commands on different replicas; execution then applies the same commands in different orders, the surviving replicas' state diverges, and a reply already produced under the old order is contradicted. That is a consensus-safety consequence (agreement and state-machine convergence), not a performance or liveness one.
participants: instance leader (owner of the instance row)
one fast-quorum peer that recomputed different attributes
recovering replica that later runs prepare for the instance
contexts: N = 3 with Thrifty (the configuration replica.New hardcodes and run.go passes through unchanged)
fast path with exactly FastQuorumSize-1 = 1 reply whose attributes differ from the leader's
leader crash after the local fast commit but before the Commit broadcast is delivered
event_paths: leader starts phase 1 for its own instance with deps d1/seq s1 and sends PreAccept to one peer
peer recomputes d2 != d1 (or s2 != s1) against its own conflict index and replies PREACCEPTED
leader adds the reply, skips the allEqual update because N <= 3 and Thrifty, and commits its own d1/s1, then broadcasts Commit
recoverer runs prepare and selects the candidate value among replies with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot
compare the (Seq, Deps) the recoverer re-commits with the vector the leader committed

scoped to project documents: the README states that the bundled EPaxos is the corrected version and that thriftiness is required for correct recovery, which suggests the N = 3 thrifty configuration was deliberately exercised (S27-readme)
unknowns: whether a recovery-led phase 1 can leave the merged committed vector's leader-row component below the peer's record, and whether the peer's larger component can be re-committed by a recovery that reaches the peer rather than the committed leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether that requires the recovering leader to have lost its own row knowledge, which the launched configuration permits only through a restart because Durable is false and no reader of the stable store exists (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos)
question.trigger_rationale: The exemption is explicit in the source: in handlePreAcceptReply the equality result computed by mergeAttributes is only accumulated in the else branch, so for r.N <= 3 && r.Thrifty inst.lb.allEqual keeps its initial true value from newLeaderBookkeeping (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S2-instance-bookkeeping). With FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2 = 2 for N = 3 (S21-quorum-sizes) and the commit condition preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1, one disagreeing reply is enough to commit the leader's own vector. The candidate pairs the commit with the recovery rule that must reconstruct the same value: handlePrepareReply keeps the attributes of the reply with the highest vbal (S15-handlePrepareReply), so two vectors at one vbal are the discriminator. A controlled multi-replica schedule is the check that could distinguish an actual same-vbal split from the author's intended majority-intersection argument.

history.question: handlePreAcceptReply commits when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and inst.lb.allEqual && allCommitted && isInitialBallot, but for r.N <= 3 with Thrifty the reply-wise equality result is discarded (the allEqual accumulator is never updated), so with N = 3 the leader fast-commits its own (seq, deps) after a single reply whose recomputed attributes may differ. Can such a commit leave two attribute vectors for one instance at the same vbal -- the leader's committed vector and the fast-quorum peer's pre-accepted vector -- so that a later recovery, which selects the reply with the highest vbal by iterating the reply slice with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot, can adopt the peer's vector instead of the committed one; and does the legal crash point between the leader's local fast commit and bcastCommit make that reachable while some replica has already executed the committed vector?
history.importance: If reachable, one instance is committed with different (seq, deps) at different replicas, so the same command is ordered differently against conflicting commands on different replicas; execution then applies the same commands in different orders, the surviving replicas' state diverges, and a reply already produced under the old order is contradicted. That is a consensus-safety consequence (agreement and state-machine convergence), not a performance or liveness one.

question.question: handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal for instance (Replica, Instance) and never writes inst.Status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept holds accepted attributes with Status NONE, and one that did see it keeps PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ. Does any decision depend on an accepted record carrying status ACCEPTED: can a later PreAccept for the same instance overwrite the accepted attributes because handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard cannot fire, and can a recovery that should re-accept an already accepted value instead take the phase-1 restart path because handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 needs a reply whose Status is ACCEPTED?
question.importance: An acceptor that stores accepted attributes without recording that it accepted them can (a) have those attributes recomputed by a later PreAccept at the same or a higher ballot instead of being preserved, and (b) hide from a recovering leader the fact that the value reached the accept phase, which is the distinction between re-proposing the accepted value and starting a fresh phase 1. Either effect can change the value a majority eventually commits for the instance, which is agreement-relevant rather than cosmetic; the accept phase is also the only place where a value is fixed without commands being stored, so a wrong reconstruction can also drop a command that only some replicas hold.

recovering replica that later runs prepare for the same instance

Does that ordering make the recovering replica's own entry raise the running ballot past every remote reply that holds the committed or accepted value at an older vbal, so that the selection ignores a committed value announced by another replica and the resolution proceeds from the local record (sub-case 6 restart, NOOP when no local command is known) instead of re-proposing the committed vector?
question.importance: If the recovering replica can ignore a remote reply that reports COMMITTED with a committed (Seq, Deps, Command) vector, recovery would re-propose a different value for an instance that some replica has already committed and may already have executed; replicas that installed the commit return early on a later Commit, so the two vectors would coexist and the state machines could diverge. That is an agreement and state-convergence consequence, not a performance one. The same rule decides whether an accepted value is re-proposed or replaced by a phase-1 restart.

question.question: When Durable is enabled, recordInstanceMetadata writes the current bal, vbal, Status, Seq and Deps of an instance into the stable store. Does the record it produces preserve the value written for bal at the offset where the recorder wrote it, or does a later write of the same record replace it, and does Status land inside the bytes a reader would use for vbal?
question.importance: A record that cannot carry the fields the writer intended hides the ballot context of an instance from any reader of that layout (a recovery path or an external tool), so a replica that restarts from such a record would be missing the value it needs to compare ballots. The consequence is bounded here because the shipped configuration passes durable=false and no reader exists in the snapshot, which is why this is recorded as an implementation-semantics defect rather than a live availability or agreement failure.

question.question: When one instance is held committed at three replicas with different committed commands for it, does applying each record through the executor leave the same effect for the instance's key, or do the replicas' state machines end up holding different effects for the same instance?
question.importance: Execution is where a committed decision becomes observable state, so an instance that is committed with different commands at different replicas produces different effects for the same key: replicas then serve different values and can never reconcile without rewriting applied state. This is the applied form of the agreement concern and is stated as its own obligation because the adopted-vector claim excludes execution.

question.question: When recovery commits a NOOP vector for an instance owned by another replica, the client operation that was attached to the original leader's bookkeeping has no owner left: handleCommit re-proposes pending proposals only when the commit lands on the replica's own row (commit.Replica == r.Id) and the commit carries exactly one NONE command, while the recovering replica's instance never held those proposals. The audit has produced twelve claim families, every analysis-root file has been read, and the map is current at version 19. Two capacities are exhausted: audit units (no further obligation can be opened) and semantic reviews (the newest artifact, the end-to-end client-reply scenario for the owner-alive re-proposal protection, executed as 6baf5b7715294d88a8f4a36e085ebd04, cannot receive the correspondence review that would confirm it). Experiments and calls remain, but the frontier is a short residual list rather than unexplored code: the reader-side reaction to a displaced stream cannot be exercised from an in-package harness because the replica package's listener is unexported; the configuration premises that decide whether the delay, durable and transitive-skip paths are active are deployment questions; and the attribution issue on the superseded C1 artifact has no mechanism the validator accepts. Unfinished units and disputes remain visible rather than being closed by this stop.

selections.rationale: First substantive product of this run: a partial but usable map of the EPaxos replica responsibility (core_overview for both core relationships, seven activities, sixteen behaviors, seven facts, ten surfaced unread boundaries) plus the first Candidate. The map is sourced only from the captured snapshot; all anomalies found while tracing the backbone are retained as open_details instead of being asserted as defects. The Candidate selects the one sourced discrepancy that would matter most if reachable: handlePreAccept stores a received command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler addresses the instance (PreAccept.Replica, Instance) named by the message.

after.purpose: Form a per-instance decision: fix the command, its sequence number and its dependency vector, and advance the instance from tentative pre-accept through accept to commit.
after.realization_summary: handlePropose allocates (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq,deps) from the local conflict tables, records the instance as PREACCEPTED and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers (Thrifty). handlePreAccept recomputes attributes on the receiver and replies with (bal,vbal,seq,deps,CommittedUpTo,status). handlePreAcceptReply merges replies and commits on the fast path when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and allEqual and (for N>7) allCommitted and the ballot is the initial ballot; otherwise the instance moves to ACCEPTED and a majority accept round runs in handleAcceptReply (acceptOKs+1 > N/2), followed by bcastCommit.

N<=3 and Thrifty skip the attribute-equality check
N>7 propagates committedDeps and can make the fast path fail on allCommitted

unknowns: whether skipping the equality check for N<=3 with Thrifty is compensated by another mechanism

after.purpose: Carry the per-instance authority context: which ballot the record is promised to, at which ballot its attributes were last fixed, and which replica may currently advance it.
after.realization_summary: Each Instance keeps bal (highest ballot promised) and vbal (ballot at which the current attributes were established). maxRecvBallot is raised by every received message type and constrains makeBallot, which picks id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and further raised while IsLeader. Ballot comparison gates every message and reply: lower ballots are dropped or nacked, and a majority of nacks lets a replica raise the ballot and run prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead it does.

unknowns: whether any in-repository caller other than a nack majority ever sets IsLeader

after.purpose: Define participant eligibility and quorum arithmetic: who is a member, who is believed alive, and how many equal or majority supports are needed.
after.realization_summary: N and F come from the peer address list and the master-visible participant count; FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2, SlowQuorumSize = (N+1)/2, WriteQuorumSize = F+1, ReadQuorumSize = N-F. formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

The wrong-slot write at epaxos/epaxos.go:809 assigns the received command to InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance], but every other access in handlePreAccept addresses the instance named by the message, (preAccept.Replica, preAccept.Instance). feedback.answered: The Candidate's discriminator is resolved on sources: no legal history in the captured snapshot establishes the branch premise. A replica that receives PreAccept can hold Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil only if some local transition sets ACCEPTED, COMMITTED or EXECUTED without also installing commands. handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but never writes Status, so an acceptor that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE even though it holds accepted attributes (S11-handleAccept). The only nil-Cmds records are fresh default records with Status NONE (S11-handleAccept, S13-handleCommit, S14-recovery-start-prepare). formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. The exposed premise is therefore whether any replica other than the leader holds the merged vector at the instance's vbal, since the leader's own record keeps the proposal ballot as vbal while a pre-accepting peer records the same pre-accept ballot (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S21-quorum-sizes, S15-handlePrepareReply).
after.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

selections.rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). In that owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum, so a recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) must intersect one of them and sees the committed vector. The exemption is therefore not automatically unsafe. The case that can split is a phase 1 restarted for an instance whose owner is another replica (handlePrepareReply sub-case 5 or 6 calls startPhase1 with PreAccept.Replica = owner and LeaderId = recovering replica, S15-handlePrepareReply, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1). There the leader and the peer both skip the owner's row but raise their own rows from their own conflict tables, so the leader can contribute a component on its own row that the peer does not have while the peer contributes another: the merged vector is then strictly greater than either record and is held only by the committing leader, while the peer keeps its smaller vector at the same ballot (S9-handlePreAccept, S10-handlePreAcceptReply).
